thread.title: Stock Market Update: S&P Inches Closer to Record Territory

title: Stock Market Update: S&P Inches Closer to Record Territory
text:
Strong: Financials, Industrials, Energy, Materials Weak: Consumer Staples, Utilities, Real Estate Moving the Market
Buying momentum after Monday's victory and five straight weekly gains for the S&P 500
Apple (AAPL) tumbles for the first time since reporting its quarterly results on July 31
Heavily-weighted financial sector outperforms as yields rise across the curve S&P Inches Closer to Record Territory 07-Aug-18 08:00 ET Market is Closed [BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: +5.80. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: +16.80.
Stocks advanced on Monday, putting the S&P 500 within 0.8% of its January 26 record high, and look poised to extend those gains at the start of today's session. The S&P 500 futures are currently trading six points, or 0.2%, above fair value, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 futures are up 17 points, or 0.2%.
Overseas, the major indices in Asia finished Tuesday broadly higher, with China's Shanghai Composite (+2.7%) -- which has struggled amid the ongoing U.S.-China trade feud -- rebounding from a more than two-year low. The major European indices are also in the green, sporting gains of around 1.0% apiece.
Looking at other markets, U.S. Treasuries are slightly lower, pushing yields higher across the curve; the benchmark 10-yr yield is up one basis point at 2.95%. Meanwhile, WTI crude futures are up 1.0% at $69.71 per barrel, and the U.S. Dollar Index is down 0.3% at 94.89, slipping from a 13-month high.
The econ calendar is light once again today with just two reports on the docket, neither of which is expected to be market-moving. The June Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey will be released at 10:00 AM ET, while the June Consumer Credit report (Briefing.com consensus $15.5 billion) will cross the wires at 3:00 PM ET.
As for earnings, Walt Disney (DIS) and Snap (SNAP) are due to report following today's closing bell.
In U.S. corporate news: Marriott (MAR 124.50, -4.78): -3.7% after below-consensus revenues overshadowed upbeat earnings. Weight Watchers (WTW 88.50, -3.71): -4.0% despite reporting above-consensus earnings and guidance. Zillow (ZG 48.69, -10.31): -17.5% after upbeat earnings were overshadowed by news that it will acquire Mortgage Lenders of America. Office Depot (ODP 2.72, +0.20): +7.9% after beating both top and bottom lines estimates.
Reviewing overnight developments: Equity indices in the Asia-Pacific region ended Tuesday on a higher note with China's Shanghai Composite (+2.7%) rebounding off this year's low. Japan's Nikkei +0.7%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng +1.5%, India's Sensex -0.1%. In economic data: Australia's July AIG Construction Index 52.0 (last 50.6) China's FX Reserves $3.12 trillion (expected $3.10 trillion; last $3.11 trillion) Japan's June Average Cash Earnings +3.6% year-over-year (expected 1.7%; last 2.1%) and June Overtime Pay +3.5% year-over-year (last 1.6%). June Household Spending +2.9% month-over-month (expected 1.7%; last -0.2%); -1.2% year-over-year, as expected (last -3.9%). June Leading Index 105.2 (expected 105.4; last 106.9) Hong Kong's FX Reserves $431.90 billion (last $431.90 billion) Singapore's July Foreign Reserves $289.20 billion (last $288.00 billion) In news: Chinese press reported that policies to increase investment and credit will be adopted soon. There has been growing speculation that the Bank of Japan may raise its short-term interest policy rate (-0.10%) before introducing larger tweaks to the overall policy stance. The Reserve Bank of Australia left its cash rate at 1.50%, as expected. Major European indices trade higher across the board with Italy's MIB (+1.2%) showing relative strength. France's CAC +0.9%, Germany's DAX +0.9%, UK's FTSE +1.0%. In economic data: Germany's June Industrial Production -0.9% month-over-month (expected -0.5%; last 2.4%). June trade surplus EUR19.30 billion (expected EUR21.40 billion; last EUR20.40 billion). June Exports 0.0% month-over-month (expected -0.4%; last 1.7%) and June Imports +1.2% month-over-month (expected 0.2%; last 0.7%) UK's July Halifax House Price Index +1.4% month-over-month (expected 0.2%; last 0.9%); +3.3% year-over-year (expected 2.7%; last 1.8%) France's June trade deficit EUR6.30 billion (expected -EUR5.60 billion; last -EUR6.00 billion) In news: Today's broad-based advance has masked a decline in Germany's industrial production in June (-0.9% month-over-month; expected -0.5%), which follows yesterday's disappointing Factory Orders report for June (-4.0% month-over-month; expected -0.3%). Italy's Deputy Prime Minister Luigi Di Maio said that senior government officials will meet tomorrow to discuss the next budget. Add this to my Page Alerts . MARKET PLACE
